user.title: Cambridge Audio CXA
user.description: Connect to the amplifier through a TCP-to-RS232 bridge (for example a USR-W610 in TCP server mode, 9600 8N1). The connection test only reads state; it does not switch the amplifier on or change anything.

data_description.model: CXA61 support follows the same documented protocol but has not been tested on hardware.
data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the serial bridge. Reserve this address in your router.
data_description.port: The TCP server port configured on the bridge.

reconfigure.title: Change bridge address
reconfigure.description: Update the bridge address. The device and entity stay the same.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the serial bridge.
data_description.port: The TCP server port configured on the bridge.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the bridge. Check the address, port and that the bridge is in TCP server mode.
error.no_response: The bridge accepted the connection but the amplifier did not answer. Check the serial cable (straight-through vs crossover), the bridge serial settings (9600 baud, 8N1) and that the amplifier has mains power.
error.rejected: The amplifier rejected the status query. Please open an issue with a probe transcript.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. See the Home Assistant log.

cannot_connect.message: Could not reach the serial bridge.

no_response.message: The bridge is reachable but the amplifier is not answering.

not_connected.message: The amplifier is not connected. The command was not sent.

timeout.message: The amplifier did not confirm the command in time. Its actual state will update when it reports.

not_confirmed.message: The amplifier answered, but reported a different state than requested.
